html:
The Sinhalese Buddhist kingdom of southwest Sri Lanka in the late 1200s and the 1300s, a time when its capital kept moving. After Polonnaruwa fell to invaders in the early 1200s, kings left the dry plains of the north, the old heartland of Anuradhapura, and moved toward the wet southwest.

The capitals in these years:

  • Dambadeniya, from about 1220;
  • Yapahuwa, a rock fortress, in the late 1200s;
  • Kurunegala, and then Gampola in the hills from 1341.

Each king guarded the Tooth Relic of the Buddha, the sign of the right to rule, and the relic moved with the court. The north of the island was held by the Tamil Jaffna kingdom. In the late 1300s the Alagakkonara family of chief ministers built a fort at Kotte, which became the capital of the Kingdom of Kotte. In 1411 the Chinese fleet of Zheng He defeated the ruler Vira Alakeshvara and carried him off to China. The map's wider label for these states is Sinhalese kingdoms.
